patch_description: The recommendation notes that single-point moves plateau around min_area ≈ 0.02 (well below the known ~0.037 optimum) because individual perturbations cannot escape local optima where the minimal-triangle constraint involves tight clusters of points. I add a simulated-annealing refinement phase that (a) with ~25% probability perturbs 2–3 nearby points simultaneously with correlated Gaussian deltas scaled to the current step size, and (b) accepts uphill moves with a standard Metropolis criterion. This lets coordinated clusters shift together. To keep the evaluator's normalization convention untouched (it normalizes by the triangle area itself), we keep raw areas. The annealing runs after the hard polish, uses a wall-clock budget for robustness, and the best-ever configuration is always kept, so failures degrade gracefully to the previous pipeline output.
